title: Chapter 696
paragraphs: Chapter 696
Episode 177. Yona, Yona, Yona... (5)
The flagship Kosyak and the 1st fleet were overpoweringly encircling the party from the air.
Jin only lifted his head to look at the fleet after Owl used the remaining threads to bind Yona.
Zipfel was not firing any cannons, but it seemed like they came to eliminate enemies rather than ally forces.
It was obvious.
In the letter Jin sent to the Zipfel side before coming to Akin, it was written that he would rescue Yona, and it also stated the defections of Hedo and Sandra.
In other words, he carried out an operation in Zipfel's territory without permission, and even pulled out key figures beforehand, so it was an incredibly uncomfortable situation for Zipfel.
Jin turned his head and looked at Hedo. He had a calm face, not seeming too bothered by the situation.
A long silence ensued. The fleet did not continue descending.

"I'm not sure how to greet since I don't know who's on the flagship. So let's skip it. But I should apologize first. I carried out the operation before getting a response because the matter of rescuing my sister was so urgent. I'll compensate for all the damage."
Jin's quiet but energetic voice resonated heavily and vibrated the sky.
The answer did not come for a long time. Everyone heard Jin's voice, but the conversations going on inside the ship were not known to those on the ground.
'Kadun seems to still be under treatment.'
If that grumpy fire dragon was here, he would have already heard a reprimand ten times over.
'Then it must be Octavia or Ronil Zipfel, but why are they hesitating? They must have already discussed how to handle Hedo before coming.'
After a few more minutes of standoff, a voice amplified by magic power finally came from the fleet.
[Lord Hedo... To be honest, until I saw you standing there myself, I did not believe the 12th generation's words. But seeing you with the 12th generation... You've really abandoned the family.]
As expected, it was Octavia. She did not hide her gloomy mood.
"Ghost captain. Leaving without a farewell has been a burden on my mind too. I'm sorry."

[I'm sorry, is that all? How many years have we been together, how many doors of life and death have we crossed together. If you were upset with the family, you should have talked to me at least. How could you suddenly betray like this? And even Sandra...!]
"Betrayal is not the right word, Ghost captain. I've never been loyal to the family in the first place."
[The family has always cherished you.]
"I know. But my only master is Miss Sandra. The family must have recognized this fact to some extent."
[Yes, we knew very well. That's why Sandra, originally an experimental subject, gained freedom due to you. No, even more than that. Sandra has been receiving special favors in every way.]
"Indeed, I am aware of that."
[Then why are you turning your blade against the family! What has bewitched you? Perhaps, were you afraid of being punished for helping the 12th during your last holiday?]
"That's right. That's part of the reason."

[This foolish...! Even if you had returned as you were, we wouldn't have investigated Sandra or pursued you. Why? Because we trusted you! We thought you were simply entangled in the 12th's trick, there's no way you could have done it intentionally... We treated you exceptionally well. So, you must at least give us a convincing reason.]
For a few seconds, Hedo looked up at the fleet.
He was reflecting on the days he spent sent from Zipfel. As Octavia said, Zipfel never wronged him.
However, the family never saw Sandra as a person.

"There was a path that could make the lady happier. Since I've spent more time in the Black Sea than in Inse, I realized it only now. The family has never regarded her as anything more than an unnecessary attachment to me. It's not about attitude and treatment, it's a matter of sincerity. If the family understood that, I would never have left."
Octavia had no response.
Of course, it wasn't because she had fully understood and accepted Hedo's position. It was because she knew that no matter what she said, he wouldn't return.
[Whatever the reason, it's the family's responsibility for failing to manage human relationships. We will respect you, Sir Hedo.]
At the new voice that followed, Jin's pupils widened.
It was the voice of Veradin. Unlike Octavia, who was barely suppressing her disturbed emotions, he had a calm tone.
"Old man."
[Let me inform you of one thing. Sandra Zipfel, due to your decision today, will inevitably become unhappy.]
Hedo did not respond.
[Jin, you must have told Sir Hedo that he can leave at any time.]
"You're so accurate, it gives me goosebumps, Veradin. Are you eavesdropping on us?"
[It's an obvious story. Also, you knew we would have to get over Hedo's betrayal because we're facing a massive public enemy.]
"I admit that."

[Therefore, I had to enforce discipline. Jin Runcandel, if Sir Hedo is not on the battlefield during the decisive battle with Rosa, we will immediately dissolve our temporary alliance. Also, Yona Runcandel, who you took so insolently today, is no exception.]
"Isn't this alliance also something that Zipfel had to make because it couldn't face Rosa alone? You talk as if we're the only ones who regret it."
[Our situation has changed, thanks to you bringing Hister to recover. Of course, it doesn't mean we don't need an alliance at all, but it's not essential anymore.]
-… These biomechanical golems can only exert their power near the sacred ground.

-Right. We are looking for a way to take them out of the sacred ground. For now, the moment they leave the vicinity of the sacred ground, they stop working like dolls with cut strings. It means they die. But I don't understand why you look so annoyed. Don't tell me you think that being a Sword Mage is a privilege only for your family?
At Veradin's words, Jin remembered the Magician's biological golems he had seen at Zipfel's sanctuary and the secret weapon of historical manipulation Ronil Zipfel had mentioned at the first meeting.
It didn't seem like they were fully prepared. If they were, they wouldn't need to make such threats.
"That's a grim warning. It doesn't seem like an empty threat, so I'll keep it in mind. Now, it looks like we've sorted out our positions, so may I ask one more thing before I go?"
[Go ahead.]
"As you can see, the Chaotic Hyperspace just exploded. We tried our best to prevent it, but were there any civilian casualties? I imagine you would have checked that much on your way here."
[No, there weren't.]
"That's a relief. Well, I'll be off. Send the compensation details to Tikan."
As Jin turned around, Zipfel's fleet began to retreat slowly. They quickly moved away, each in their own direction.
When Jin met Veradin in the sanctuary, and even now, he couldn't see any aspect of the Veradin he knew.
It felt like he had regained his family but lost a friend.
'I need to find that guy someday, like Sister Yona... But it won't be easy.'
He wanted to return quickly, start the purification, and have a conversation with his returned sister. That was the only comfort right now.
In the Sword Garden.
Rosa was looking down at her eldest son with an emotionless face.
[Joshua... You've wasted my power again, and fled like a dog.]
Joshua had lost his physical form five times in the battle with Bale. Each time, Rosa's energy was depleted, and Joshua had used her power without her permission.
Joshua, kneeling on one knee, couldn't even dare to lift his head.
After being dragged up from the underground prison, Joshua was captivated by the belief that he could accomplish anything.
He thought there wouldn't be any more disappointments for his mother. He had become the second-generation again, and the power of the monstrous gift from his mother was infinitely vast.
Even his mother, unlike when she caused his fall, showed signs of expectation. It was like she was saying that she would help him, and he should beat the youngest.
[Mother, I...]
[I've never had a son like you. Address me correctly.]
But nothing had changed.
He was still the youngest, breaking his mother's expectations, and the briefly good atmosphere after his return was already steeped in frustration.
[I apologize, Lady.]
[Yes, you have a mouth to speak after all. Try to explain again, what made you fail this time?]
He had no answer.
Whether the plan was not meticulous, the given power was insufficient, or there were other variables. None of them could possibly convince his mother.
An unspeakable self-loathing was boiling inside him.
Joshua truly felt like he was less than trash in a back alley.
[I have nothing to say.]

[When I pulled you out of the underground prison, I thought you had changed. That's why I gave you power and entrusted you with a task. It wasn't a difficult thing. It was to kill Dante using Yona's clones, and torment the youngest.]
Seeing his mother call Jin 'the youngest' even though he was not a son, felt like reviving the nightmare of his fall.
[Please... give me one more chance.]
[Why should I? Even with my power, the youngest remains a wall you cannot overcome. This has already been proven.]
He could not answer any question.
He was having trouble breathing. So when Joshua let out a gasping breath unknowingly, like a man drowning, Rosa coldly shook her head.
[Go back to the underground prison until I call you. From now on, Diphus will take your place.]
Joshua turned around with a vacant look, and Ilina followed him.
Ilina comforted Joshua, saying she would somehow postpone the execution, and he should calm down and wait a bit.
After sending Joshua off, Ilina returned to Rosa and let out a deep sigh.
“When I was working through Joshua, his incompetence made me so angry, I thought I'd go mad. But that ended up being helpful to you, Lady. Fate is... quite amusing.”
[If he was the youngest, he would have realized my intention and resisted early on. That this ridiculous charade is a play.]
The only reason Rosa pulled Joshua from the underground prison was simple.
“Yes, that dull character won't understand his role until he disappears.”
Joshua’s intense despair, which he had built up over time and was still diligently nurturing, was all that Rosa needed from him. Hence, for the first time, Rosa saw Joshua as a useful figure.
He was bound to keep despairing, no matter what abyss he fell into. Through the 'prophecy', his only hope.
